status: Draft indicator set for expert review (Phase B). Wording and anchors are expected to change after review; the dimension structure and scoring equations follow the working paper.

scale.0: None: no evidence the practice exists
scale.1: Nascent: ad hoc, person-dependent, or planned only
scale.2: Partial: documented and in use for some critical services
scale.3: Managed: documented, owned, covering all critical services, reviewed on a schedule

not_applicable: Use null with a justification; N/A indicators are excluded from m_d in equation (1).

dimensions.name: Crypto inventory & dependency map
dimensions.definition: Completeness of algorithm, key, certificate, and library inventory across critical services.

indicators.text: An inventory lists where public-key cryptography is used in each critical service (TLS endpoints, VPN, PKI, code signing, HSM-backed keys, payment messaging, database encryption).
anchors: Documented inventory for some critical services
Complete, owned inventory refreshed at least annually
indicators.evidence: Inventory extract (redacted), owner, last refresh date

indicators.text: For each use, the algorithm, key size, and protocol version are recorded (e.g. RSA-2048, ECDSA P-256, TLS 1.2).
Third-party and embedded cryptography (vendor appliances, core banking, mobile SDKs, card/POS, HSM firmware) is included with vendor and version.
anchors: All vendors and versions tracked with contract owner

indicators.text: Discovery is tool-assisted (network scanning, certificate transparency, code/dependency scanning, CBOM) rather than only interview-based.
indicators.evidence: Tool name, scan scope and date

dimensions.name: HNDL exposure & data longevity
dimensions.definition: Classification of data/secrets by confidentiality lifetime vs. expected quantum-relevant horizon.

indicators.text: Data classes carry a required confidentiality lifetime (e.g. KYC records, health records, state secrets, long-term contracts).
anchors: Confidentiality lifetime for key data classes
Lifetime set for all classes and linked to the crypto inventory

indicators.text: Flows that carry long-lived data over public-key protected channels are identified (the harvest-now targets).
anchors: Mapped for all flows, with traffic volumes

indicators.text: The organisation has stated a planning assumption for when a cryptographically relevant quantum computer could exist, and uses it in decisions (Mosca: shelf-life + migration time vs. horizon).
anchors: Assumption documented, reviewed annually, and drives prioritisation

indicators.text: HNDL is recorded as a risk in the enterprise or ICT risk register with an owner and treatment.
anchors: Recorded, treated, and reported to the board/risk committee

dimensions.name: Crypto-agility & hybrid readiness
dimensions.definition: Ability to swap algorithms, run hybrid handshakes, and avoid hard-coded classical suites.

indicators.text: Algorithms and parameters are set through configuration or a crypto service/library abstraction, not hard-coded in applications.
Critical TLS/VPN stacks can negotiate hybrid key exchange (e.g. X25519MLKEM768) or have a dated upgrade path to it.
PKI and HSMs can issue, store, and use PQC or composite keys/certificates (vendor-confirmed or tested).
There is a tested procedure to rotate algorithms and keys across a service within a defined time.

dimensions.name: Technical performance envelope
dimensions.definition: Whether PQC object sizes and latencies fit operational SLOs (informed by lab M1-M9).

indicators.text: Latency and size budgets (SLOs) are known for the critical protocols: handshake time, message size limits, MTU, certificate chain size, smart-card/HSM storage.
anchors: Documented for all, with headroom calculated

indicators.text: PQC performance has been measured on the organisation's own or representative hardware (e.g. with the KC-LAB-PQC harness) rather than taken from vendor claims.
anchors: Measured on production-representative hardware, results on file

indicators.text: Constrained endpoints are identified and assessed (POS terminals, USSD/SMS gateways, smart meters, IoT, low-bandwidth branches).
anchors: Listed with a PQC fit/no-fit decision per class

indicators.text: Middleboxes and network paths are tested for larger handshakes (fragmentation, ClientHello over one packet, firewall/IDS/load-balancer behaviour).
anchors: Tested on all critical paths, issues tracked

dimensions.name: Governance, skills & vendor path
dimensions.definition: Board/CISO ownership, staff competence, procurement clauses, and vendor PQC roadmaps.

indicators.text: A named executive owns the quantum-safe transition and reports progress to the board or risk committee.
anchors: Named owner with periodic board reporting

indicators.text: Staff responsible for PKI, networks, and development have PQC training appropriate to their role.
Procurement and contracts require vendors to state PQC support and a migration timeline (FIPS 203/204/205).
anchors: Clause in new and renewed contracts, tracked

indicators.text: Regulatory and sector expectations are tracked (e.g. CBK, CA Kenya, ODPC, national cybersecurity guidance; NIST IR 8547 deprecation dates for vendors).
anchors: Tracked and mapped to the plan

dimensions.name: Migration programme maturity
dimensions.definition: Existence of phased plan, pilots, rollback, and monitoring for quantum-safe transition.

indicators.text: A phased migration plan exists with priorities derived from D1 inventory and D2 exposure.
At least one pilot (e.g. hybrid TLS on an internal service, PQC code signing in test) has been run and evaluated.
anchors: Pilot evaluated and promoted to production

indicators.text: Rollback and interoperability fallback are defined for each migration step.
anchors: Defined and tested for each step

indicators.text: Progress is measured (share of critical flows on hybrid/PQC, inventory coverage) and reviewed.
anchors: KPIs tracked and reviewed on a schedule

references: NIST IR 8547 (initial public draft), Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards, November 2024
NIST SP 1800-38, Migration to Post-Quantum Cryptography (NCCoE practice guide)
CISA, NSA, NIST, Quantum-Readiness: Migration to Post-Quantum Cryptography, August 2023
Mosca, M. Cybersecurity in an era with quantum computers: will we be ready? IEEE Security & Privacy 16(5), 2018
